stories.title: The judge used to be the user
stories.summary: AI has collapsed the middle of model building, and the people who once defined what is correct have gone with it.

stories.title: Can AI generate good designs from raw user data?
stories.summary: Researchers tested whether AI could design interfaces using raw user comments versus synthesized findings. The model produced better results when provided with pre-processed recommendations. It appears that even when delegating design to software, the quality of the input remains a factor.

stories.title: Qualitative user-research methods: An overview
stories.summary: This guide details four common qualitative research methods, including usability testing and diary studies. It serves as a companion to a quantitative overview, noting that costs and difficulty remain relative to specific project needs and tools. Qualitative research focuses on understanding behaviors and experiences.

stories.title: UX Roundup: GPT-6.2 | Prepare with AI | Speed | Unambitious Academics | AI Permission Requests | Permissions Barrage | R
Post-discharge cardiometabolic app meets usability hurdles among older adults
stories.summary: A mobile platform designed to assist older patients with cardiometabolic conditions during hospital-to-home transitions showed marginal usability. A study of 110 participants in China identified significant initial learning hurdles for the target demographic. The tool was intended to simplify complex disease management.

stories.title: Digital tool for inflammatory bowel disease therapy demonstrates good usability
stories.summary: A web-based decision aid, I(BD) SELECT, showed good usability and acceptability during alpha testing with patients and clinicians. Developed for the Belgian healthcare market, the tool aims to support complex treatment choices for individuals managing inflammatory bowel disease.

stories.title: The product page is the new packaging
stories.summary: Zocket uses AI to automate the creation of Amazon A+ content and marketplace assets. The company argues that brands have outgrown manual, asset-by-asset production. By using approved visual rules, the system generates thousands of banners and tiles to match a brand's catalogue.

stories.title: Starbucks’ viral Bearista cup is back for the holidays
stories.summary: The Starbucks Bearista Glass Cold Cup has returned, triggering collector demand and long lines at store openings. The handblown, bear-shaped cup features a green beanie and striped straw. The release has resulted in reports of physical altercations at some locations.

stories.title: Emiglia brand identity by Another Collective
stories.summary: Another Collective rebranded a Porto pasta maker by unifying its factory and bar under one voice. The studio retained existing illustrations while introducing a typographic layer and a warm tomato-red color palette. The goal is to ensure tradition reads as confidence.

stories.title: Polar’s utilitarian graphic design system for P.A.C. Bakery
stories.summary: São Paulo studio Polar created a reactive design system for P.A.C. bakery that avoids formal logos in favor of typed letters and receipt menus. Because two of the studio's founders are partners in the bakery, the identity adapts daily to the business's physical space.

stories.title: Book design: Accidental Collage by Dr.Me & Waiting Room Press
stories.summary: A 400-page book documenting weathered street posters arrives intentionally damaged. Manchester studio Dr.Me hand-ripped every cover to mimic the billboard strata featured inside. The design choice intends to evoke the aesthetic of city walls before the reader even opens the spine.

stories.title: The book design of ADI Design Museum’s Compasso d’Oro
stories.summary: Leonardo Pertile designed a 1,040-page monograph documenting seventy years of Italian industrial design. The work is split into twin cloth-bound volumes, color-coded in brick-red and yellow. The scale of the project reflects the history of the collection.

stories.title: How Studio Herrström reimagined the Milkshake brand identity
stories.summary: Stockholm label Milkshake updated its identity to emphasize car culture. The studio redrew the brand's splash mark as a rounded symbol and introduced high-visibility colors. The design system uses road sign aesthetics and typography that fills the frame to reflect the brand's origins.

stories.title: Award-winning motion design and typography projects
stories.summary: Jatin Joshi, an MFA student at Rochester Institute of Technology, received awards for his motion poster series and illustration work. His projects, including a visual identity system for a music festival, were recognized in an international competition for emerging creative talent.

stories.title: Web design: Petrillo Studio’s interactive chronometer
stories.summary: Petrillo Studio replaced standard portfolio thumbnails with a live, red chronometer on its homepage. The design uses oversized black numerals and draggable clock hands to display the time. The interface functions as an interactive instrument rather than a traditional gallery.

stories.title: Branding: Zero 10 brand identity by Saffron
stories.summary: Saffron created a brand identity for Art Basel's Zero 10 project using a frame-like mark inspired by a 1915 show. The system uses two numerals with open space between them to frame digital art. The branding is designed to label the work and disappear.

stories.title: Allo, the free variable typeface that redraws Inter for interfaces
stories.summary: Josh Puckett released Allo, an open-source variable typeface based on Inter 4.1. The font includes three variable axes for weight, roundness, and optical size. It features 606 glyphs and was redrawn to provide a warmer character for digital design projects.

stories.title: Pen.dev aims for the design workflow
stories.summary: Pen.dev combines a 60fps WebGL canvas with live shaders and two-way MCP integration. The team at Abduzeedo reports the tool has replaced Figma in their daily flow, citing impressive speed and a familiar environment for those accustomed to browser inspectors. It is designed to feel like building real products.

stories.title: Canva cuts staff as it seeks a refound
stories.summary: Canva is cutting or relocating up to 1200 roles, representing more than one-fifth of its workforce. Chief executive Melanie Perkins stated the firm needs to be refound following a year of slowed growth. The company insists that human tasks will not be replaced by its artificial intelligence tools.

stories.title: AI agents move into text messaging
stories.summary: A growing number of AI agents now function via text message, allowing users to schedule appointments, research trips, or shop online without downloading new apps. While Instinct holds a $10 billion valuation, numerous other agents are competing to manage these tasks directly through existing mobile messaging services.

stories.title: Personal agents shift toward shopping
stories.summary: Personal agents like Meta’s Muse are increasingly taking action on behalf of users by scanning email inboxes. More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada used Muse in its first six weeks, with shopping cited as the primary use case. Artificial intelligence now influences nearly one-third of purchases.

stories.title: OpenAI updates prompting for Astra and Sol
stories.summary: OpenAI has released new prompt templates for its GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models to address issues with brief answers and unnecessary questioning. The company advises developers to let models make assumptions rather than interrupting workflows. Parameters like temperature and top_p have been removed from the API.

stories.title: Canva added an AI ‘kill switch’ to its tools - Fast Company
Canva adds an AI kill switch
stories.summary: Canva has introduced two new toggles for Free and Pro users to hide generative AI features and reduce AI-generated content in its template library. The company has spent years integrating generative AI into its platform, and these settings now allow users to opt out of the experience.

stories.title: Figma faces challenges with AI code integration
stories.summary: Figma's latest AI tools allow developers to bring code into design canvases using the Model Context Protocol. Lead engineer Aditya Muttur notes that maintaining consistent performance across diverse, user-imported codebases remains an unresolved engineering challenge. Providing a baseline level of speed for these workflows is the current focus.

stories.title: Mystery AI Model Gestalt Tops Design Leaderboard in Blind Test, Beating Human Designers with Elo of 1,931 - BigGo Financ
Troubleshooting Canva loading issues
stories.summary: To resolve loading errors in Canva, users are advised to check for service outages, reopen browser tabs, or try a private window. If the editor reports being offline, the company recommends maintaining the connection until the platform confirms that all changes have been saved to the server.

stories.title: Creating QR codes in Canva
stories.summary: Canva allows users to generate static or dynamic QR codes through its Apps or Elements menus. Static codes are intended for fixed destinations, while dynamic codes permit URL changes after creation. Both options are available across all plans, though dynamic features may vary based on the specific subscription.

stories.title: Workbrew 2.0 tracks unapproved software
stories.summary: Workbrew 2.0 serves as an inventory tool for development software installed by employees without administrative approval. The platform aims to help Mac administrators track applications on their fleet, providing visibility into the software that developers have added to their devices outside of standard management deployments.

stories.title: Virse integrates AI models into design workflows
stories.summary: Virse has launched a node-based Creative Canvas that connects design system drafting, brand style guides, and Ideogram 4.0 layout generation. The workspace allows teams to coordinate assets across 40 different AI models, aiming to finalize visual direction before moving into code or print production templates.

stories.title: Figma promotes Specs for workflow management
stories.summary: Figma is highlighting its Specs feature and AI agent as a container for project context. By bringing diagrams, designs, and technical decisions onto a single canvas, the company claims teams can better compare prototypes and collaborate on implementation plans. The goal is to keep scattered information in one place.

stories.title: Stitch Loop automates software fixes
stories.summary: Stitch Loop is a Google AI agent designed to monitor metrics and automatically ship software fixes. The tool is currently being discussed as part of the company's broader efforts to integrate autonomous agents into development workflows.

stories.title: Smorza manages Mac audio output
stories.summary: Smorza is a utility that allows users to assign individual volume and output settings to specific Mac applications. The software is currently being discussed as a solution for managing audio routing on macOS.

stories.title: Core77 weekly design roundup
stories.summary: The latest Core77 roundup highlights various industrial design consultancies and product development agencies. Featured firms include ANDESIGN, Bould Design, Doris Dev, Studio RedEye, Acorn Product Development, and Tactile, covering work across locations ranging from Silicon Valley to New York and Hong Kong.

stories.title: Editing video with AI in Adobe Premiere
stories.summary: Adobe Premiere allows users to edit video by deleting words from generated transcripts. Additional AI features include audio enhancement, auto-ducking, automatic captioning, and Generative Extend for lengthening clips. The software is licensed for commercial use and exports videos without watermarks for professional and creative projects.

stories.title: The Senator Group India launches Kaya seating
stories.summary: The Senator Group India has introduced its Kaya office seating collection, developed with design studio Pearson Lloyd. The company says the range addresses the requirements of modern, flexible workspaces by offering an alternative to conventional task chairs that rely on multiple technical adjustments. It is a chair.

stories.title: MeitY updates domestic value calculation rules
stories.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has revised its domestic value addition framework for six IT hardware categories, including laptops and servers. The new methodology uses a Bill of Materials based mechanism to calculate local content. The government says this will promote indigenous manufacturing and innovation.

stories.title: Blue Bath Gallery opens flagship store in Delhi
stories.summary: Blue Bath Gallery has launched a flagship store in Delhi in association with the India Today HOME show. The event featured representatives from TOTO and various architects, focusing on international design and contemporary living. The gallery aims to celebrate materiality and style in the capital city.

stories.title: Ameet Mirpuri on his two-decade design practice
stories.summary: Designer Ameet Mirpuri has operated his studio for 24 years, maintaining a rule to never repeat himself. While managing roughly 65 concurrent projects across India and abroad, he avoids what he describes as the copy-paste exercise of imported marble and predictable moods in luxury interiors.

stories.title: Kids Rooms India on bedroom design
stories.summary: Hyderabad-based studio Kids Rooms India offers guidance on planning children's bedrooms to balance storage with play space. The firm suggests that the secret to managing an ever-expanding inventory of toys and furniture lies in careful planning long before the actual design work begins.

stories.title: Chennai home moves away from minimalism
stories.summary: A 4,000 sq ft residential project in Chennai has been designed to reject stark minimalism in favour of tactile textures and vintage undertones. The project for a young family of four aims to prioritise comfort and memory, reflecting a broader shift toward emotional nostalgia in interior design.

stories.title: Josephine Estate restored in Goa
stories.summary: The 100-year-old Josephine Estate in Goa has been restored by Isprava to bridge architectural heritage with contemporary living. The project preserved the original name inscribed on a ceramic tile, framing the renovation as a dialogue between the estate's historic character and modern requirements.

stories.title: Luminous rebrands with solar focus
stories.summary: Luminous Power Technologies has unveiled a new logo and the tagline Har Soch Mein Power. The company says this marks its evolution into a comprehensive consumer energy solutions provider, with solar energy at the centre of its growth strategy. It remains an inverter and battery brand.

stories.title: NCL Industries adopts new corporate logo
stories.summary: NCL Industries has adopted a new corporate logo, filing a disclosure under SEBI regulations on November 20, 2026. The company confirmed the change does not alter its name, legal status, or business operations. Both the old and new logos will be used during a transition period.

stories.title: Redbrick Offices raises Rs 630 crore
stories.summary: Managed workspace provider Redbrick Offices has secured Rs 630 crore in equity across its Series A and A1 rounds. The funding was led by India SME Investments and Abakkus Asset Manager. The company had previously operated as a bootstrapped business for several years.

stories.title: Prabhkiran Singh launches AI assistant Save8
stories.summary: Former Bewakoof CEO Prabhkiran Singh has launched Save8, an AI-powered tool for comparing prices across ecommerce platforms. Singh is reportedly seeking external capital for the venture, though he did not respond to inquiries regarding his business model or specific fundraising plans at the time of publication.

stories.title: GG Technologies sues Apple over NameDrop
stories.summary: GG Technologies has sued Apple in the Bombay High Court, alleging that the NameDrop feature infringes on a patent it holds for contact-sharing technology. The startup, founded by an IIT Delhi alumnus, claims it developed the underlying technology years before Apple introduced its version in 2023.

stories.title: Sarvam AI launches Token Factory platform
stories.summary: Sarvam AI has launched a commercial platform allowing developers to access multiple AI models through its computing infrastructure. The Bengaluru-based startup says the move addresses the growing demand for AI inference, as Indian companies look to move beyond basic data centre and GPU investments.

stories.title: Scaler cofounder unveils AI data venture Arcfront
stories.summary: Scaler cofounder Anshuman Singh has launched Arcfront, a venture that converts professional problem-solving records into training data for AI models. Singh claims four frontier AI labs became customers within a year of operations, though he did not name the labs or provide specific revenue figures.

stories.title: Celcius Logistics seeks Rs 100 crore funding
stories.summary: Cold-chain logistics provider Celcius Logistics is in talks to raise Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C round. The company plans to use the capital to scale its pharma and hyperlocal businesses. Existing investors including IvyCap Ventures and Omnivore are expected to participate in the round.

stories.title: River Mobility revenue grows as losses widen
stories.summary: Electric two-wheeler maker River Mobility reported a 4.2X increase in operating revenue to Rs 432.3 crore for FY26. During the same period, the startup's net loss widened 46 percent to Rs 285.7 crore as it ramped up production and sales of its scooters.

stories.title: Knit Health raises $35 million for AI model
stories.summary: Healthcare AI startup Knit Health has raised $35 million in Series A funding to deploy its Med-BEAM model. The company describes the technology as a healthcare world model designed to predict patient care needs by analysing clinical decisions. Total funding for the firm now stands at $46.6 million.

stories.title: Battery startup naturenix raises $3.02M Series A to scale fast-charging tech - Dealroom
Fashion design and communication courses compared
stories.summary: Fashion Design focuses on creating garments, silhouettes, and physical collections. Fashion Communication centres on branding, visual merchandising, and digital storytelling. While both fields exist within the fashion industry, one produces the product and the other produces the experience around it. The distinction remains largely aesthetic.

stories.title: NID DAT 2027 exam topics outlined
stories.summary: The National Institute of Design Design Aptitude Test evaluates drawing skills, visualisation, and creative problem-solving. The examination covers areas including object drawing, product development, and visual storytelling. These topics are intended to help candidates organise their preparation for the 2027 cycle.

stories.title: NID and Thapar University teams win AAKRUTI 2026 India finale
stories.summary: Student teams from NID Andhra Pradesh and Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology won the India finale of the AAKRUTI 2026 Innovation Competition. Each team received a trophy and 50,000 rupees. They will represent India at the global finals in Nashville this February.

stories.title: Healthcare solutions win AAKRUTI 2026 India challenge
stories.summary: Dassault Systèmes named teams from NID Andhra Pradesh and Thapar University as winners of the AAKRUTI 2026 competition. The teams were recognised for developing healthcare solutions, including a device designed to assist seniors with ear drop application. They now advance to the global stage.

stories.title: design/leader: Jen Yuan, Partner at View Source - Design Week
Type Directors Club announces jury presidents for TDC73
stories.summary: The Type Directors Club has appointed Paulina Reyes, Jen Mussari, and Irene Vlachou to lead the juries for its 73rd competition. The presidents will oversee communication design, lettering, and type design categories. The full jury lineup is expected to be announced in January 2027.

stories.title: SVA offers course on brand identity design
stories.summary: The School of Visual Arts is offering a continuing education course on brand identity, priced at 450 dollars. The curriculum covers logo design, visual elements, and the development of a brand voice for print and packaging. Students will complete projects to explore these principles.

stories.title: Adobe brand strategy discussion
Studio job listings reach 78 openings
stories.summary: Crunchyroll, Electronic Arts, and Rodeo FX are among the studios currently listing 78 open roles. Positions range from engineering and data to VFX and animation. The listings cover studio locations from Montreal and London to Shanghai.

research.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
research.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend.
